patch_description:
This proposal keeps the paper's fixed feature map and re-uploading layout but refactors the ansatz block to be more parameter-efficient and motif-aware. It:

- Encodes geometric symmetry by grouping corner/edge/center local rotations while allowing a single shared center phase (pre/post) to reduce redundant parameters.
- Preserves a CZ lattice backbone for robust short-range entanglement but augments it with targeted controlled-phase (CRZ) interactions between center and edges to focus global center modulation.
- Allocates explicit three-qubit ZZZ motifs aligned with the eight winning lines (horizontal, vertical, diagonal) plus a shared doubly-controlled CCRZ diagonal phase to boost sensitivity to diagonal patterns.
- Reuses a small, structured set of parameters across wires where symmetry is beneficial, yielding 13 parameters per block (78 total) — fewer parameters than the baseline and aligned with prior good performers — while keeping expressive three-qubit motifs to improve generalization on winning-line detection.

The block is compact (lower parameter count), structured for motif discovery (explicit ZZZ/CCRZ on win lines), and maintains the same external inputs/outputs as the original program.
